Load-bearing beyond display: Relic.is_tradable (sts2_rl/relics/base.py:126-136) excludes has_upon_pickup_effect relics, mirroring RelicModel.IsTradable, so Whetstone is correctly barred from the trade events even though its pickup effect is not implemented.

AfterObtained.maps_to: NO COUNTERPART -- the port is a behaviourless stub (whetstone.py has no methods at all)
AfterObtained.issue: Rollup of guards G1 and N1 per binding rule 4. Whetstone.cs:20-29 upgrades CardsVar(2) randomly chosen upgradable ATTACKS in the deck; the port upgrades nothing and consumes no Niche draw.

guards.what: G1 (LIVE): the port implements no pickup effect at all, and the premise behind the stub is false -- after_obtained IS dispatched
guards.issue: MECHANISM: Whetstone.cs:22-27 is `Deck.Cards.Where(c => c != null && c.Type == CardType.Attack && c.IsUpgradable).ToList().StableShuffle(Rng.Niche).Take(Cards.IntValue)` then CardCmd.Upgrade on each -- two random upgraded Attacks, permanently. whetstone.py declares only id/name/rarity/has_upon_pickup_effect and its docstring justifies that with 'an out-of-combat deck edit, so this is a no-op stub'. PROMPT.md bug class 12 applied: the premise is false. Relic.after_obtained is a real base hook (sts2_rl/relics/base.py:138-141) and RunState.add_relic calls it on EVERY granted relic (run.py:552); .superpowers/sdd/content-relic-sweeps.md's sweep C lists this unit in the 'out-of-combat pickup effect, stub' family and reports a LIVE dispatch site for it. REACHABILITY (LIVE, executed -- py audit/tools/relic_probes_b17.py upgradestubs): `run.add_relic('whetstone')` changes 0 deck cards, where C# would upgrade 2 Attacks (the Ironclad starting deck holds 5 Strikes and a Bash, all Attacks and all upgradable, so the effect is available from floor 0). The CONTROL in the same probe is decisive: `run.add_relic('neows_talisman')` upgrades 2 deck cards through the same run.py:552 dispatch (sts2_rl/relics/neows_talisman.py:29-33) -- and one of the two is a Strike, i.e. exactly a card Whetstone would have taken -- so the pipeline is not merely present but already used by a ported relic to do this. Both sides ported: Common in the grab bag, and the deck is a first-class run object. Observable in RL play (2 permanently upgraded Attacks) and in conformance (sts2_rl/conformance/runner.py:618 compares the deck as (id, upgrade_level) pairs). PROMPT.md bug class 29 checked, not assumed: this relic and war_paint are NOT the same unit with a swapped constant -- they differ in the card TYPE filter (Attack vs Skill) and both are audited on their own merits here, with the same verdict because both ports are equally empty. Rule 7: sts2_rl/relics/base.py, run.py, sts2_rl/relics/neows_talisman.py, sts2_rl/conformance/runner.py and .superpowers/sdd/content-relic-sweeps.md are NOT hashed by this record.

guards.what: N1 (LIVE for RNG parity, dormant for RL): `StableShuffle(Rng.Niche)` names an explicit stream and the stub consumes none
guards.issue: PROMPT.md bug class 16's second half, and the same mechanism this batch records at relic/war_hammer N2 and relic/war_paint N1 -- one verdict per mechanism (binding rule 3). The shuffle is genuinely CONSUMED in C# (StableShuffle always draws, unlike the `claws` case class 16 warns about), so a run that picks up Whetstone shifts every later Niche consumer's position. Distinct from G1: an implementation that upgraded the first two Attacks in deck order would close G1 and leave this open. Rule 7: audit/records/relic/war_hammer.json and audit/records/relic/war_paint.json are NOT hashed by this record.

guards.what: N2: `c.Type == CardType.Attack && c.IsUpgradable` and the `c != null` null-guard (Whetstone.cs:22)
guards.issue: Recorded so a fix does not lose the filter. `IsUpgradable` is what keeps PROMPT.md bug class 14 from firing -- the sim's Card.upgrade() is a bare `upgrade_level += 1` (sts2_rl/cards/base.py:146-147) with no guard, and 18 ported Curses and 14 Statuses have max_upgrade_level 0. The Attack type filter alone would already exclude Curses and Statuses, but a fix that filtered on type and forgot IsUpgradable would still be wrong for any Attack already at its max upgrade level -- and unlike War Paint's Skill filter, Attacks are the type the sim's own transform and reward paths generate most, so the upgraded-Attack case is common. Carries G1's LIVE label as part of the same missing implementation; no independent observable. Rule 7: sts2_rl/cards/base.py is NOT hashed here.

guards.what: N4: `undo_after_obtained` is absent from this port
guards.rationale: PROMPT.md v6 binding item 3: the helper has no C# counterpart, so a port lacking it is not diverging from the source. Same operational constraint on the fix as relic/war_paint N4: once G1 is implemented the pickup mutates the deck permanently, and the conformance runner's relic swap calls undo_after_obtained on a dropped relic (sts2_rl/conformance/runner.py:461, :694), which cannot un-upgrade a card. A tooling constraint on the fix, not a fidelity gap. Rule 7: sts2_rl/conformance/runner.py is NOT hashed here.
